title: Le grand frisson de Mathias  (Mathias's Big Thrill)

segments.t: Following his alarming alcohol blackout after the previous night's celebrations, Mathias meets assistant Noémie at a quiet Parisian restaurant. Relieved to find him safe and sound, Noémie admits her frantic worries before their private conversation takes an unexpectedly romantic and secretive turn. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
Mathias! Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
Oh, je suis tellement désolée...
Laisse, Noémie.
J'étais tellement inquiète.
J'ai appelé tous les hôpitaux, puis les pompiers.
Tu dois me prendre pour une folle.
Comme tu viens d'une famille de bâtisseurs, tu peux tout réparer.
Nathalie Baye a appelé.
Je lui ai dit qu'on avait un accord pour son contrat.
Oui, merci.
J'en ai vu de toutes les couleurs. Mais pas comme vous.
Des amants qui font semblant de trinquer au lieu de s'embrasser?
Je n'ai jamais vu ça!
Chut!
Oh, Mathias...
Le grand frisson. Allons-y, maintenant.
Let's walk through the secret dinner of Mathias and Noémie step by step.
Mathias! Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
'Mathias! What are you doing here?' Literally 'What is it that you do there?'. Noémie uses the casual 'you' since they are close. In French, this sounds very fluent.
Oh, je suis tellement désolée...
'Oh, I am so sorry...' Noémie apologizes. She adds a subtle sound to 'sorry' because she is talking about herself. The French use this structure often.
Laisse, Noémie.
'Don't worry, Noémie.' Literally 'Léave'. Mathias tells her to let it go with a gentle command. In French, this phrasing is common.
J'étais tellement inquiète.
'I was so worried.' Noémie describes her past feelings. The action word refers to a continuous state in the past. You will find this useful in French.
J'ai appelé tous les hôpitaux, puis les pompiers.
'I called all the hospitals, then the firefighters.' Noémie lists her actions. The expression for 'hospitals' changes entirely when there is more than one. This sounds extremely natural in French.
Tu dois me prendre pour une folle.
'You must take me for a crazy person.' Literally 'take me for a crazy'. Noémie changes the shape of 'crazy' to match herself. In French, this is perfectly fine.
Comme tu viens d'une famille de bâtisseurs, tu peux tout réparer.
'Since you come from a family of builders, you can fix everything.' Mathias uses 'like' to mean 'since' or 'because' at the start of a thought. A standard way to speak in French.
Nathalie Baye a appelé.
'Nathalie Baye called.' Noémie reports a completed action. She builds it using 'has' followed by the action. In French, you will hear this.
Je lui ai dit qu'on avait un accord pour son contrat.
'I told her we had an agreement for her contract.' Literally 'I to her have said'. Noémie puts the target right before the action. The French say this often.
Oui, merci.
'Yes, thank you.' Mathias keeps his reply soft. This is an everyday expression of gratitude. In French, this is quite common.
J'en ai vu de toutes les couleurs. Mais pas comme vous.
'I have seen all sorts of things. But not like you.' Literally 'I have seen of all the colours'. The waiter uses a colorful idiom for seeing crazy things. This is how you say it in French.
Des amants qui font semblant de trinquer au lieu de s'embrasser?
'Lovers pretending to toast instead of kissing?' Literally 'who make seeming'. The waiter points out their funny fake toast. A handy phrase in French.
Je n'ai jamais vu ça!
'I have never seen that!' The waiter speaks in the negative. He wraps the action with two pieces meaning 'never'. A useful expression in French.
Chut!
'Hush!' Mathias quiets him down. You can say this handy sound to ask for silence. This is very typical in French.
Oh, Mathias...
'Oh, dear Mathias...' Noémie speaks fondly. She drops the 'dear' entirely, letting her tone show it. A common chunk in French.
Le grand frisson. Allons-y, maintenant.

'The big thrill. Let's go now.' Mathias uses a handy chunk to say 'let's go there'. It shows they are leaving together. You will hear this in French. Now listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.
Mathias! Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
Oh, je suis tellement désolée...
Laisse, Noémie.
J'étais tellement inquiète.
J'ai appelé tous les hôpitaux, puis les pompiers.
Tu dois me prendre pour une folle.
Comme tu viens d'une famille de bâtisseurs, tu peux tout réparer.
Nathalie Baye a appelé.
Je lui ai dit qu'on avait un accord pour son contrat.
Oui, merci.
J'en ai vu de toutes les couleurs. Mais pas comme vous.
Des amants qui font semblant de trinquer au lieu de s'embrasser?
Je n'ai jamais vu ça!
Chut!
Oh, Mathias...
Le grand frisson. Allons-y, maintenant.
Mathias and Noémie share a tender romantic secret away from the pressures of the agency, heading off into the Parisian night together. See you next time!
Bonne soirée!
